conventions.convention: Continuous Stokes uses real V=H1_0(D;R^d), Q=L2_0(D), the velocity gradient norm, b(v,q)=-∫q div v, and aν(u,v)=2ν∫ε(u):ε(v), with ν>0 and a nonempty bounded connected Lipschitz domain in dimension two or three. H1_0 means Sobolev closure of compactly supported smooth functions.
The Bogovskii kernel uses a unit-integral smooth bump supported in a ball with respect to which U is star-shaped; all input data and resulting vector fields are real.
The Fourier transform is the negative-sign 2π normalization, so differentiation corresponds to multiplication by 2πiξ_j.

MINI uses exactly tiled polygonal/polyhedral domains, conforming shape-regular affine simplices in dimensions two and three, scalar bubble (d+1)^(d+1) times the product of barycentric coordinates, zero-boundary continuous P1 velocities plus vector cell bubbles, and continuous mean-zero P1 pressures.

Face-average interpolation selects an incident facet at each interior vertex and an incident boundary facet at each boundary vertex; coefficients are dual facet moments rather than point evaluations of H1 functions.
Fortin preservation is equality of pressure pairings, not pointwise equality of divergences; the weak discrete kernel and the almost-everywhere divergence-free kernel are distinct definitions.
Mixed Galerkin quasioptimality assumes coercivity on the discrete kernel Z_h, positive β_h, and nonzero V_h and Q_h; continuous-kernel coercivity alone is not its hypothesis.
Countable Choice is explicitly assumed for the Hilbert inf-sup right-inverse theorem and its Hilbert-space existence argument.

load_bearing.statement: Let D⊂R^d be nonempty, bounded, connected and Lipschitz, with d∈{2,3}. Under Countable Choice there is a bounded linear map B_D:L2_0(D)→H1_0(D;R^d) such that div B_Dq=q and ‖∇B_Dq‖₂≤C_div(D)‖q‖₂. The constant is finite and independent of any finite-element mesh.

Under Countable Choice, on a bounded connected Lipschitz polygonal/polyhedral domain with a conforming shape-regular simplicial mesh in dimension two or three, the specified face-average interpolant maps H1(D) to continuous P1, preserves H1_0, is uniformly H1-seminorm stable, has local L2 error at most Ch_K‖∇v‖ over the vertex patch, and has local H1 error at most Ch_K‖D²v‖ for H2 inputs.

On the mini-element spaces there is a Fortin operator Π_h:V→V_h preserving b(v,q_h) for every q_h∈Q_h, with ‖Π_hv‖_V≤C_F‖v‖_V. C_F depends only on dimension and mesh shape regularity, not h; consequently β_h≥(C_F C_div(D))^(-1).

Under Countable Choice, bounded real bilinear forms on real Hilbert spaces, positive inf-sup, and coercivity on the closed constraint kernel give a unique solution of a(u,v)+b(v,p)=F(v), b(u,q)=G(q), for every bounded F and G, with the displayed α, β and M_a stability bounds; the Q={0} case reduces to Lax–Milgram.

For bounded open U star-shaped with respect to a ball, under Countable Choice the specified Bogovskii integral extends boundedly and linearly from L2_0(U) to H1_0(U;R^d), with div B_Uf=f and ‖∇B_Uf‖₂≤C_U‖f‖₂, using the displayed finite derivative-bound constant.

Under Countable Choice, for smooth compactly supported φ and ρ>0, the integral from zero to infinity of 2π|ξ_j||φ̂(tξ)| is at most ρ^(-1)‖φ‖₁+ρ‖∂²_jφ‖₁. The specified distributional T operator restricted to bounded open U has the displayed L2 bound A_j(φ), and extends uniquely to L2(U).
Under Countable Choice, for bounded open D and v∈H1_0(D;R^d), 2‖ε(v)‖₂²=‖∇v‖₂²+‖div v‖₂², hence ‖∇v‖₂≤√2‖ε(v)‖₂.

Under Countable Choice, a continuous mixed solution, nonzero conforming finite-dimensional spaces with β_h>0, and discrete-kernel coercivity imply unique Galerkin solvability and the displayed velocity and pressure bounds U_h,P_h for every pair of approximants, retaining β_h explicitly.

concerns.concern: The Statement says “let b:V×Q→R be bounded” but does not require bilinearity, whereas Given explicitly assumes “a bounded bilinear form” and the proof uses linearity to construct B*, apply Lax–Milgram, and obtain a linear right inverse. Boundedness alone does not imply the claim: take V=Q=R and b(v,q)=vq/(1+|v|). Then |b(v,q)|≤|v||q|, the displayed β equals 1, and the defining identity gives Bv=v/(1+|v|), whose range is (-1,1), so B is not onto. The essential bilinearity hypothesis needs to appear in the Statement.

seams_checked.note: Checked Darcy wellposedness, RT0/P0 divergence lift, and Darcy error citations against the actual suppliers. They retain Countable Choice, connected Lipschitz geometry, the H1_0 lift, the negative divergence pairing, graph-norm conversion via Poincare, and discrete-kernel coercivity. One-cell zero spaces are treated separately.

Checked the model, pressure-gauge lemma, displacement theorem, mixed MINI definition, and uniform mixed theorem. They preserve the pressure sign, zero-mean divergence, homogeneous Korn identity, continuous inf-sup hypotheses, and exact MINI mesh class. The additional pressure penalty and its endpoint cases are handled locally.

Checked the Stokes-space, Korn, divergence-lift, interpolation, Fortin, mixed-error, and discrete-projector interfaces in the flow consumers. The weak MINI kernel remains distinct from exact incompressibility. Stronger Fortin approximation estimates are derived in local lemmas; the mass projector is used for L2 best approximation, without importing an H1 stability claim. Pressure recovery uses the lift with the correct sign and mean-zero gauge.

The two-level P1 Poisson stable-decomposition theorem cites the face-average interpolant with its actual dimension, Countable Choice, zero-boundary, shape-regularity, local L2 approximation, and H1-seminorm stability hypotheses. Its cube meshes satisfy those hypotheses.
